newsitem.title: UK: Screamin' Lord Sutch offers reward to get car back.
newsitem.headline: Screamin' Lord Sutch offers reward to get car back.

text.p: Screamin' Lord Sutch, Britain's longest-serving political party leader, put up a five-million "loony pound reward" on Monday after his campaigning "loonymobile" was stolen.

"I am lost without it. This is a disaster," said the head of the Official Monster Raving Loony Party who had hoped to use his fluorescent red car to campaign in the Uxbridge by-election on London's western fringes.

But the newly overhauled car was stolen from outside his London home and Sutch, desperate to get it back, even offered the thieves a copy of his autobiography and his most recent CD -- as long as they promised not to play it.
Sutch, a rock singer who campaigns in leopardskin tailcoat and top hat, heads the most colourful and durable of Britain's multitude of fringe groups who always add colour to election campaigns.
Before he went into politics, Sutch ran a rock band called The Savages in which stars such as Keith Moon of The Who and guitar legend Jeff Beck played early in their careers.
